findings.description: The journey model makes consumer optional, but the objective requires declaring the intended consumer family for consumer-facing outcomes. If omission remains valid, typing and consumer-surface validation can be bypassed before close-time enforcement ever sees stable vocabulary.
findings.recommendation: Pin whether consumer is required for all readiness-gated journeys, or define an explicit legacy/default path that cannot satisfy this objective's completion tests.

findings.description: The seeded evidence rule depends on fixture_only, but the plan only says fixture_only is optional and does not pin its default. Missing fixture_only semantics can make seeded_masks_readiness nondeterministic for older or partially-authored journeys.
findings.recommendation: Define fixture_only default explicitly, preferably false, and require tests for omitted fixture_only on seeded-only evidence.

findings.description: The typing function is specified for one surface_class, but journeys can declare multiple surfaces and consumer=both. The plan does not pin journey-level aggregation semantics that require at least one human-surface requirement and at least one agent-surface requirement to be satisfied together.
findings.recommendation: Add a deterministic journey-level derivation rule: validate declared surfaces, derive requirements per surface, then conjunct the required groups for all surfaces needed by the consumer declaration.

findings.description: The structured_error rule depends on a degraded or error-path claim, but claim_kind is otherwise closed to read_only, mutation, and qualitative. There is no pinned input field that tells the pure typing rule when an error path is being evaluated.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit error_path or outcome_mode input, or extend and test the closed claim_kind vocabulary if that is intended.

findings.description: The mutation requirement notation is ambiguous: the prose says idempotency plus rollback are both required, but the requirement-expression example could be read as alternatives or as malformed grouping.
findings.recommendation: Specify mutation as two conjunctive groups, for example [{idempotency}, {rollback}], appended to the base surface requirement.

findings.description: F004 says degraded_dishonest only when neither family provides availability=unavailable for a required data_source, but the user journey requires both human and agent families to degrade honestly. One family could silently omit its degraded signal while the other family masks the failure.
findings.recommendation: For consumer=both, require an honest unavailable signal from each applicable family, then separately compare shared structured fields for disagreement.

findings.description: The checker needs to compare human and agent EvidenceRefs by data_source, but EvidenceRef does not gain an explicit surface_class, consumer_family, or source-family attribution field. Inferring family from evidence_class is underspecified and breaks for shared classes such as structured_error.
findings.recommendation: Pin where family attribution lives: on EvidenceRef, on the containing journey/surface binding, or on a typed evidence-source wrapper, then test mixed-family evidence sets.

findings.description: F004 adds allowed_degraded_modes to the contract but never specifies how the checker validates or consumes those modes. That leaves an accepted schema field with no behavioral effect in the honesty gate.
findings.recommendation: Define allowed_degraded_modes as either enforced policy or remove it from this plan; if enforced, add tests for allowed and disallowed degraded modes.

findings.description: The CLI transcript adapter is required to be non-interactive and no live paid call may be made, but the plan does not pin the command contract, fixture mode, or environment guard that prevents accidental paid external execution.
findings.recommendation: Define a deterministic fixture-safe CLI invocation for tests and require the adapter to fail closed or typed-skip when only paid/live execution is available.

findings.description: The contract names the typed-skip reason-location fix as D028, while F003 labels the same acceptance point as D029. This drift can cause implementers to miss the exact round-3 typing fix the objective says is in scope.
findings.recommendation: Normalize the decision identifier for typed-skip reason location across the plan before implementation starts.

findings.description: F002 references a close gate named F005 even though close-time enforcement is explicitly out of scope and delegated to sibling plan 2b. This creates an implementation target that is not part of the objective contract.
findings.recommendation: Replace the F005 reference with the sibling 2b close-time enforcement plan and state that this plan only emits typed advisory results.
